faq.q: Can I start numbering at a page other than 1, or from a different number?
faq.a: Yes, both. The "Start number" box sets what the first numbered page is labelled — set it to 5 and the sequence runs 5, 6, 7… The "Pages to number" box controls which pages actually get a stamp: type all, a range like 3-10, or a list like 1,4,6. There is also a "Skip first page (cover)" checkbox that leaves page 1 blank while still numbering the rest, which is the usual choice for a document with a title page.

Five: a plain number (1), "Page 1", "1 of N", "Page 1 of N", and "- 1 -". The "of N" formats use the total count of pages that are actually being numbered and the start number, so if you number pages 3-10 starting at 1 the last page shows "8 of 8". You also choose the position (bottom or top, left/center/right), the font size in points, the margin from the edge, and the colour.

faq.q: Will the number land correctly on a page that is rotated or a different size?
faq.a: Yes. Each page is measured on its own, so a file that mixes A4, Letter and landscape pages gets its number placed against the correct edge of every page. Pages that carry a /Rotate value are handled in their visual orientation — the tool works out where the bottom-right (or whichever corner you picked) is after rotation and draws the number there, upright, rather than in the unrotated corner.

faq.q: How do I check the placement before downloading?
faq.a: A live preview rendered with pdf.js shows page 1 and, if it differs, the first page that will actually be numbered, with the number drawn on top exactly where it will appear. As you change position, format, size, margin or colour the preview updates, so you can confirm the look before clicking Add Page Numbers & Download. The output is saved with the standard Helvetica font via pdf-lib and downloads as your-file-numbered.pdf; nothing is uploaded.
